gaps.sentence: She carried a suitcase in ___ hand.
gaps.explanation: 'Each hand' views the two hands individually; 'every hand' is not used for body parts this way.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room for another desk in here.
We see our grandparents ___ other weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other weekend' means alternate weekends; 'each other' has a different, reciprocal meaning.

gaps.sentence: ___ candidate was given five minutes to speak.
gaps.hint: one at a time, singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each candidate was given' — singular agreement; 'all candidate' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: The hall was so crowded that ___ found a seat.
gaps.hint: a crowded hall means no one succeeded
gaps.explanation: 'So crowded that nobody found a seat' matches the logic of the sentence; 'anybody' cannot be the subject of an affirmative clause.

gaps.sentence: She gave the children two sweets ___.
gaps.hint: distribution per child at the end of the sentence
gaps.explanation: 'Two sweets each' means two per child; 'every' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ in a bad mood.
gaps.explanation: 'Mostly' is an adverb meaning mainly or usually; 'most' as a quantifier needs a noun.

gaps.sentence: There is so ___ crime in this area that people are afraid.
gaps.explanation: 'So much' is used with uncountable nouns like crime; 'plenty' would need 'of'.
